To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chloro- and bromoacetamidid derivatives are potent inhibitors of the PNGase.

the inhibitory activity of glycosyl chloroacetamides is dependent on the N-acetyl group of the reducing sugar and that the reactivity and position (reducing end) of the leaving group are important factors.
haloacetamididoligosaccharides are potential inhibitors of cytosolic peptide:N-glycosidase and that their inhibitory activity is affected by the position of the leaving groups and N-acetyl groups.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel class of PNGase inhibitors that may be used as tools to study the biological functions of PNGase and to investigate the mechanism of the deglycosylation process.
the synthesis and inhibitory properties of haloacetamido oligosaccharides toward cytoplasmal peptide:N-glycosidase.
the synthesis and inhibitory evaluation of haloacetamidyloigosaccharide analogs as inhibitors of cytoplamic peptide:N-glycosidase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the inhibitory potency of haloacetamido oligosaccharides depends on a balance between reactivity, leaving group ability and recognition by the enzyme.
the N-acetyl group at the reducing terminus of chitobose is the most important recognition element of the PNGase substrate.

the N-acetylglu- cosamine moiety of the chitobioose unit is essential for recognition of the substrate by PNGase and that the halogenoacetamide moiety of the N-acet- ylglucosamine unit is important for the inhibitory activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a haloacetamido group at the reducing terminus of chitobiosyl oligosacchride derivatives is a promising candidate for PNGase inhibitors.
the N-acetyl group of the reducing GlcNAc and the chloro leaving group at the C-2 position of the nonreducing GlcNAc are essential for PNGase recognition.
the N-acetylglu- cosaminyl residues at the reducing end of the chitobioose derivatives are important for the inhibitory activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chloroacetamido group is a suitable leaving group for inhibiting PNGase.
haloacetamidid derivatives are potential PNGase inhibitors, and their activity can be modulated by the nature of the leaving group, the position of the leaving groups, and the number of sugar units.
the chloroacetamido group is the best choice for the synthesis of glycosyl inhibitors for PNGase.
